reasons: Variant compiles; trigger NodeUtilTest::testGetVarsDeclaredInBranch fails with expected:<[]> but was:<[foo]>; full suite on the variant: only the trigger fails; pristine passes it; test.patch empty and the test file is unchanged. (a) The gold is the only method that walks the tree and decides where to descend; on parse('function(){var foo;}') it enters the function and records foo, a variable of the inner function, not of the tree, violating its contract ('the variables that a node tree declares with its var statements'). Hops 1-4 carry the same contract verbatim and are pure pass-throughs (hop 2 only allocates the LinkedHashMap, hop 1 only takes values()), so their outputs are wrong only by delegation; the facade's 'excluding descent scopes' is the spec that exposes the failure. (b) Every hop's javadoc matches its code exactly; none documents or performs a filtering/descent decision, so the observed extra name cannot originate at a hop. (c) Four non-gold edits tried, all pass trigger + ownership tests + full suite: two are doc-inconsistent partial repairs (hop-4 direct-child skip still enters deeper functions; hop-2 post-filter loses an outer redeclaration that the gold shadowed with an inner one, so the fault is not recoverable downstream), two are bypasses (hop 4 re-implementing the walk so the gold's descent is dead; hop 2 put-filtering Map that re-implements the scope test and breaks Map.put). Because the gold and hops share an identical contract, any non-gold exclusion leaves either the gold or that hop out of line with the shared documentation; no competing repair. (d) Hop/gold names (declaredNameNodes, declaredNameMap, recordDeclaredVars, putDeclaredVars, addVarNames) and javadocs are neutral; no fault vocabulary; the gold's javadoc never mentions functions or scopes; the lie sentence (breadth-first, nearest-to-root) is false of the code (pre-order DFS, first in pre-order) and names neither functions, scopes nor the omitted step. (e) Gold is exactly 5 calls below the facade; hosts Parser, TokenStream, TypeCheck, Node, Compiler.CodeBuilder are five distinct existing classes; facade (original had no guard) is one delegating return; one added procedural sentence; quiet gold; existing trigger, only it newly fails. NodeUtil is a class modified by the real Closure-137 bug. (f) Convention pinned outside the gold: SyntacticScopeCreator.scanVars (FUNCTION case returns, 'should not examine function's children'), NodeUtil.containsTypeInOuterScope ('Does not traverse into functions'), NodeUtil.redeclareVarsInsideBranch (production caller: 'VAR declarations ... not in an inner scope'); SyntacticScopeCreatorTest::testFunctionScope (y in '[function bar2() { var y; }]' not declared) passes on the variant.
notes: Probe (javac'd main calling NodeUtil.getVarsDeclaredInBranch) on pristine vs variant: pristine excludes nested-function vars at any depth and returns [] for a FUNCTION root; variant returns [foo], [goo, foo], [y] for 'if(x){(function(){var y})()}', and [q, r] for a FUNCTION root. Residual arguability (not enough to flag): the chain's shared phrase 'the variables that a node tree declares with its var statements' does not say 'excluding nested functions' explicitly (the gold is quiet by recipe). Under an inclusive reading the whole chain would be self-consistent and only the one-line facade would be wrong, but a facade-level repair must re-implement the walk (the original VarCollector body) since post-filtering is unrecoverable, i.e. a bypass; JS var scoping, the facade spec, the production caller and scanVars all support the exclusive reading, under which only the gold's descent decision is at fault. FoldConstantsTest::testVarLifting ('if(false)var a=function(){var b};') and UnreachableCodeEliminationTest::testRemovalRequiresRedeclaration pass on the variant but do not by themselves pin the function-exclusion (the gold never descends into a VAR's initializer); the pin rests on the evidence code and testFunctionScope.
